review_scope: FRANK/ClayCode shared-ancestry assumptions touching commit/replay semantics

items.assumption: Critical effects need explicit authority/recovery/replay evidence rather than trusting model intent or a storage side effect.
items.independent_discriminator: Local SQLite concurrency experiment plus primary SQLite transaction semantics.
items.reason: The independent mechanism probe supports moving replay identity checking into the commit serialization domain, but does not independently validate broader FRANK architecture or cognition claims.
items.counterhypothesis: Storage uniqueness alone can provide equivalent safety with less protocol machinery.

items.assumption: ClayCode requires a new DB/idempotency-specific core syntax primitive to close concurrency replay races.
items.independent_discriminator: Post-lock typed fingerprint/replay mechanism probe using existing host/runtime constructs.
items.reason: No new core syntax was needed for the tested slice. Preserve existing typed IR and enforce a lowering/runtime legality contract unless a harder executable counterexample falsifies this.

items.assumption: An idempotency key collision can always be treated as a valid replay.
items.reason: The uniqueness-only control suppressed the write but could not classify semantic mismatch. Replay requires operation/payload identity binding or equivalent proof.
